title: Absolute value of a complex number
statement:
For a complex number $z=x+iy$ with $x,y\in\mathbf R$, its *absolute value* is

$$
|z|=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\in\mathbf R_{\geq0},
$$

the nonnegative square root of $z\bar z=x^2+y^2$. It satisfies $|zw|=|z|\,|w|$, $|z|=0$ if and only if $z=0$, and $|z|$ is the usual absolute value when $z\in\mathbf R$.
